items.stimulus: In traditional Japanese woodblock printing, the artist's design was transferred to several blocks of cherry wood, and a separate block was carved for every color. A single landscape print might require a dozen of these ______ one had to line up exactly with the others, or the colors would overlap and blur the image's fine edges.

items.explanation: "A single landscape print might require a dozen of these blocks" is a complete sentence. "Each one had to line up exactly with the others..." is also a complete sentence. A comma plus the FANBOYS word "and" is a correct way to join two sentences, so this is the answer.

per_choice.correct: The text before the blank is a full sentence; the "while" clause and the phrase "sealed with clay stoppers" are only add-ons to it. "The team concluded..." is a second full sentence. A comma followed by the FANBOYS word "so" is a legal way to join two full sentences, and "so" fits the logic: the different contents led to the conclusion. That makes choice A correct.
per_choice.B: You knew the second clause expressed a result, so you added "therefore." But "therefore" is an adverb, not a conjunction. Putting commas around it doesn't change that two full sentences are joined by only a comma, which is a comma splice.
per_choice.C: You chose the right joining word but put the comma on the wrong side. Between two full sentences the comma goes before "so," not after it, and "so" with no comma in front leaves the sentences fused.
per_choice.D: You treated "therefore" as if it could join clauses the way "so" does. It can't, so this choice is still a comma splice between two full sentences. Swapping in a FANBOYS word or a semicolon would fix it.
